ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The open-loop logarithmic magnitude-frequency characteristic \( L_0(\omega) \) of a unity feedback system is shown in Figure 6-5. A series compensator is added with the transfer function:

\[
G_c(s) = \frac{\left(\frac{s}{3} + 1\right)\left(\frac{s}{10} + 1\right)}{\left(\frac{s}{0.3} + 1\right)\left(\frac{s}{100} + 1\right)}
\]

What is the transfer function \( G_0(s) \) of the system before compensation?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a broken-line asymptotic diagram of the open-loop logarithmic amplitude-frequency characteristic L0(ω), with the vertical axis being L0(ω) dB and the horizontal axis being the logarithmic scale of frequency ω. The curve decreases at -20 dB/dec in the low-frequency band, and it can be read that the amplitude at ω=1 is about 40 dB, and at ω=10 is about 20 dB. The slope of the curve changes to -40 dB/dec at ω=10, and then the slope further changes to -60 dB/dec at ω=100. Reasoning: The initial slope is -20 dB/dec, indicating that the open-loop transfer function contains an integrating element, that is, contains the factor 1/s. At ω=10 rad/s, the slope changes from -20 dB/dec to -40 dB/dec, indicating that a first-order inertial pole is added here, corresponding to the factor s/10+1, that is, 0.1s+1. At ω=100 rad/s, the slope changes from -40 dB/dec to -60 dB/dec, indicating that another first-order inertial pole is added here, corresponding to the factor s/100+1, that is, 0.01s+1. Let the open-loop transfer function of the uncorrected system be G0(s)=K/[s(0.1s+1)(0.01s+1)]. From the initial asymptote in the figure, L0(1)=40 dB at ω=1; in this section it is approximately K/s, so 20log10 K=40, obtaining K=100. What the question asks is G0(s) of the system before correction, so the given series correction device Gc(s) is not multiplied into it.

method.method_draft: First describe the plotted magnitude characteristic. From the initial -20 dB/dec slope, infer one pole at the origin, so the transfer has a factor 1/s. From the slope becoming -40 dB/dec at ω=10, infer a first-order pole at 10 rad/s, written as (s/10+1)=(0.1s+1). From the slope becoming -60 dB/dec at ω=100, infer another first-order pole at 100 rad/s, written as (s/100+1)=(0.01s+1). Use the plotted value L0(1)=40 dB on the initial asymptote: for K/s, 20log10 K=40, hence K=100. Since the text asks for the system before compensation, take the plotted L0 as the uncompensated open-loop characteristic and do not include Gc(s). Therefore write G0(s)=100/[s(0.1s+1)(0.01s+1)].

Image description: The figure shows a broken-line asymptotic diagram of the open-loop logarithmic amplitude-frequency characteristic L0(ω), with the vertical axis being L0(ω) dB and the horizontal axis being the logarithmic scale of frequency ω. The curve decreases at -20 dB/dec in the low-frequency band, and it can be read that the amplitude at ω=1 is about 40 dB, and at ω=10 is about 20 dB. The slope of the curve changes to -40 dB/dec at ω=10, and then the slope further changes to -60 dB/dec at ω=100.
Reasoning: The initial slope is -20 dB/dec, indicating that the open-loop transfer function contains an integrating element, that is, contains the factor 1/s. At ω=10 rad/s, the slope changes from -20 dB/dec to -40 dB/dec, indicating that a first-order inertial pole is added here, corresponding to the factor s/10+1, that is, 0.1s+1. At ω=100 rad/s, the slope changes from -40 dB/dec to -60 dB/dec, indicating that another first-order inertial pole is added here, corresponding to the factor s/100+1, that is, 0.01s+1. Let the open-loop transfer function of the uncorrected system be G0(s)=K/[s(0.1s+1)(0.01s+1)]. From the initial asymptote in the figure, L0(1)=40 dB at ω=1; in this section it is approximately K/s, so 20log10 K=40, obtaining K=100. What the question asks is G0(s) of the system before correction, so the given series correction device Gc(s) is not multiplied into it.
